literal: Nature is for asceticism one-thing not-having; possession delusion becomes again having-brought-back.
translation: The true nature of asceticism is to possess absolutely nothing. Owning anything will bring back delusion once again.
modern: ஒரு பொருளும் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதே துறவுக்கு இயல்பாகும். ஒரு பொருளை உடைமையாகக் கொண்டாலும் அது மீண்டும் மயக்கத்தைக் கொண்டுவரும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core requirement of renunciation ('நோன்பு') as the complete absence of possessions ('ஒன்று இன்மை'). It contrasts this state of having nothing with ownership ('உடைமை'). The word 'மயல்' refers to the delusion or confusion of worldly attachments. The text warns that retaining even a single possession will bring back ('பெயர்த்து') this delusion once again ('மற்றும்'), thereby undoing the ascetic's progress.
